question: Which entry scrolls an object to an absolute y on this image, so a page whose content shrank can be put back at the top?
prototype_hypothesis: void lv_obj_scroll_to_y(lv_obj_t *obj, lv_coord_t y, lv_anim_enable_t anim_en)
callsite_evidence: sub_C2BD7F0 is the same shape as the recovered scroll_to_x: lv_anim_del(obj, scroll-y exec), cur = lv_obj_get_scroll_y(obj), lv_obj_scroll_by(obj, 0, cur - y, anim).
sub_C2BD700 is the shared lv_obj_scroll_by; the Lua `scroll_to` binding calls the x sibling for both x and y (a firmware copy-paste), so the y entry is only reachable from C.
ownership_analysis: The object keeps its own scroll state; the call only moves its children.
unsafe_assumptions: Scroll animation is disabled by passing 0 as the last argument.
recommended_probe: Open a confirmation dialog from a scrolled overview page and check that the title is at the top.
